This document defines confidence levels for BITwiki content. These are markers of our current assessment, not fixed truths. The epistemic tier system provides a structured framework for communicating the evidentiary status of knowledge claims within the BITwiki ecosystem, enabling readers to make informed judgments about the reliability and maturity of presented information.

The framework draws upon established epistemological traditions, including the philosophy of science (Popper, 1959; Kuhn, 1962), social epistemology (Goldman, 1999), and contemporary knowledge management theory (Nonaka & Takeuchi, 1995). By explicitly marking confidence levels, we acknowledge the provisional nature of empirical knowledge while maintaining rigorous standards for claim validation.
